## What did you build?

<div class="process-line" aria-label="Completed HMM to prediction chain">
  <div class="step">HMM edges</div><div class="join">→</div>
  <div class="step">$\Pr(w)$</div><div class="join">→</div>
  <div class="step">$\eta^{(w)}$</div><div class="join">→</div>
  <div class="step">$F_x$</div><div class="join">→</div>
  <div class="step emph">belief geometry</div><div class="join">→</div>
  <div class="step">future predictions</div>
</div>

<div class="grid-3">
<div class="card blue"><h3>Linear propagation</h3><p>Matrix products sum hidden paths.</p></div>
<div class="card orange"><h3>Nonlinear step</h3><p>Normalization depends on the current belief.</p></div>
<div class="card purple"><h3>Change of view</h3><p>Geometry is the same posteriors seen as points and maps.</p></div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
- Target: about 90 seconds.
- Ask students to supply each arrow verbally before revealing your summary.
- Protect this synthesis even if the morning ran long: it is the dependency bridge to the afternoon.
:::

## Two machines answer two questions

<div class="grid-2">
<div class="card blue">
<h3>Hidden Markov model</h3>
<p><strong>Question:</strong> how can a latent mechanism generate the observable stream?</p>
<p><strong>State:</strong> hidden phase $S_t$.</p>
<p><strong>Dynamics:</strong> symbol-labelled stochastic edges.</p>
</div>
<div class="card purple">
<h3>Mixed-state presentation</h3>
<p><strong>Question:</strong> how does an observer update uncertainty from the symbols?</p>
<p><strong>State:</strong> reachable posterior $\eta^{(w)}$.</p>
<p><strong>Dynamics:</strong> normalized maps $F_x$.</p>
</div>
</div>

<div class="takeaway">The MSP is an inference process induced by the generator—not another hidden physical machine.</div>

::: {.notes}
- Target: about 90 seconds.
- Invite one student to state the difference without using the word “state” alone.
- Emphasize histories are labels for MSP states; equal posteriors are the same MSP point.
:::

## One normalization creates the observer dynamics

<div class="equation-panel">
$$
\underbrace{\pi T^{(w)}}_{\text{unnormalized forward row}}
\quad\xrightarrow{\text{sum}}\quad
\Pr(w)=\pi T^{(w)}\mathbf 1
\quad\xrightarrow{\text{normalize}}\quad
\eta^{(w)}=\frac{\pi T^{(w)}}{\pi T^{(w)}\mathbf 1}.
$$
</div>

After a new symbol $x$ arrives, reuse the posterior as the next prior:

$$
F_x(\eta)=\frac{\eta T^{(x)}}{\eta T^{(x)}\mathbf 1}.
$$

<div class="grid-2">
<div class="card green"><h3>Before normalization</h3><p>Matrix propagation is linear.</p></div>
<div class="card orange"><h3>After normalization</h3><p>The denominator bends straight mixtures into nonlinear dynamics.</p></div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
- Target: about 2 minutes.
- This is recap, not a fresh derivation. Ask what the denominator means: the probability of observing $x$ under the current belief.
- Keep row-vector orientation consistent with the notebooks.
:::

## Repeated Bayes maps carve predictive geometry

<div class="figure-frame medium">
<img src="assets/generated/mess3_recursive_geometry.png" alt="Mess3 simplex showing nine length-two posterior points and thousands of seven-symbol reachable posteriors forming a nested fractal set.">
</div>

<div class="takeaway">Three hidden generator states define the ambient triangle—not the number of reachable observer beliefs.</div>

::: {.notes}
- Target: about 2 minutes.
- Left: composition nests images. Right: iteration reveals the limiting visual structure.
- Every dot is a posterior belief, not a physical hidden state and not a token embedding.
:::

## Same next token, different future

<div class="grid-2">
<div>
$$
\eta^{(01)}=(0,0,1),\qquad
\eta^{(10)}=(1/2,1/2,0).
$$

Both give

$$
\Pr(X_{t+1}=0,1\mid h)=(1/2,1/2),
$$

but disagree over two-token futures.

<div class="takeaway">The current next-token vector is not generally sufficient as the <em>sole recursively retained state</em>.</div>
</div>
<div class="figure-frame short">
<img src="assets/generated/z1r_future_comparison.png" alt="Bar chart comparing two-token future distributions after histories 01 and 10. The distributions differ despite identical one-step predictions.">
</div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
- Target: about 2 minutes.
- State the quantifier carefully: this is a result about a sole recursive next-token state.
- Ask which two-token test most visibly separates the two histories.
:::

## What follows—and what does not

<div class="grid-3">
<div class="card green">
<h3>Established</h3>
<p>A chosen HMM posterior is sufficient to predict every future word generated by that realization.</p>
</div>
<div class="card gold">
<h3>Qualified</h3>
<p>Belief coordinates are model-relative and may contain redundant distinctions.</p>
</div>
<div class="card orange">
<h3>Not established</h3>
<p>A full-prefix transformer need not persistently store this posterior; it can recompute or use other predictive coordinates.</p>
</div>
</div>

<div class="handoff">
<span class="label">Afternoon puzzle</span>
<p>If next-token training rewards future-sensitive computation, what trace—if any—should that leave in transformer activations?</p>
</div>

::: {.notes}
- Target: 1–2 minutes plus questions.
- Use remaining time for unfinished exercises and questions; this slot is intentionally a buffer.
- The first claim is sufficiency relative to a chosen realization, not automatic minimality for the observable process.
:::
